title: Automated recovery playbooks for common Private VPC healthcheck failures
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Create a set of operational playbooks and automated remediation hooks for the top recurring Private (VPC) deployment healthcheck failures. Scope includes: authoring human-readable runbooks, implementing IaC-safe remediation actions (Terraform/Terragrunt modules or orchestrated apply), wiring remediation to alerting/monitoring (Prometheus/Datadog), and safe fail-open policies for customer traffic. Acceptance criteria:

- 3 canonical runbooks covering the most common failures (control-plane connectivity, subnet/NAT misconfig, and service-auth token expiry) with step-by-step troubleshooting and roll-forward/rollback guidance.
- Fully automated remediation implemented for at least 2 failures (control-plane reconnect + token refresh) with audit logs and a reversible plan.
- Terraform modules or automation scripts checked into infra-private-modules repo with CI gating and feature-flagged rollout.
- Integration tests and chaos test plan demonstrating remediation does not worsen partial outages.
- Operational dashboards and one-click telemetric telemetry links included in each runbook.
runbook_samples:
Control-plane unreachable (Private agent cannot reach Redwood control plane):
1) Verify VPC route table and IGW/NAT status in console. 2) Check security group egress rules for control plane CIDR (10.0.0.0/16) and ephemeral ports. 3) On host: curl -v https://control.redwood-internal/api/health -> capture TLS handshake error. 4) If route missing, apply terraform module 'private-network-fixes' to re-add route and run 'terraform plan' -> 'terraform apply' in dry-run mode first. 5) If TLS error, rotate host CA bundle and restart agent service. 6) Post-fix: run healthcheck endpoint, confirm agent re-registration, and annotate incident ticket.

NAT / egress path saturated or misconfigured (agents time out on external calls):
1) Inspect NAT gateway metrics and CloudWatch/Datadog egress error spikes. 2) Confirm private-subnet route to NAT gateway exists. 3) If NAT gateway is throttled, toggle autoscaling of NAT (if using NAT instances) or provision additional NAT gateways via 'infra-private-modules/nat-scale' terraform module. 4) Apply CIDR-level egress rate-limiting temporarily to protect control-plane links. 5) Run smoke tests to validate external dependency calls succeed.
automated_remediation_playbooks:
Auto-reconnect flow for control-plane failures:
- Trigger: alert from heartbeat aggregator when >3 agents in a region report 502s for control API for 2m.
- Orchestrator: remediation-runner service posts a ‘reconnect job’ to infra-ops queue.
- Action sequence: 1) Verify route table entries via terraform state. 2) If missing, run 'terraform apply' with module 'private-network-fixes' using a generated plan and operator approval window (30s) unless 'auto-approve' flag is enabled for low-risk customers. 3) After apply, validate TLS handshake and agent re-registration. 4) Emit audit: PR link, terraform plan diff, operator id, timestamp.
- Safety: Plan diffs stored and reversible via 'terraform destroy' of applied resources where safe.

Token refresh and rotation remediation:
- Trigger: service-auth token expiry detected by auth-proxy healthcheck.
- Action sequence: 1) Initiate non-blocking token rotation via 'secrets-rotation' module that creates a new token with limited scope. 2) Gradually switch agent pool to new token using rollout policy (10% -> 50% -> 100%). 3) If rollout fails, automatically rollback to previous token and create incident. 4) Log all rotations to KMS audit trail and Confluence rotation log.
implementation_notes: Prefer implementing remediation as idempotent Terraform modules rather than ad-hoc scripts to ensure state is authoritative.
Use feature flags for enabling fully automated apply in sensitive customer VPCs; default to operator-approved plan apply.
Include a 'canary' execution mode for remediation-runner that executes in dry-run and notifies operators before performing changes.
All automation must emit structured audit events to our internal event-bus and create a GitHub PR with the terraform plan attached for traceability.
testing_plan: Unit tests: terraform plan generation and policy checks with tfsec/policy-as-code.
Integration: deploy sandbox VPC and inject control-plane failures via iptables rules; assert remediation-runner heals within SLO in >=90% of trials.
Chaos: schedule a 2-hour chaos window to randomly remove routes/NAT gateways and validate playbooks do not cascade-fail other customers.
